# Draft:TACA Awards

The Thali Architecture & Construction Awards (commonly known as TACA or the Thali Awards) is an annual industry recognition platform based in Tamil Nadu, India. Established in 2026 by the architectural media platform Thali Connect, the award is notable for being one of the first in the region to honor the entire ecosystem of the construction industry, including civil engineers, contractors, artisans, and masons, alongside architects.
The awards ceremony is typically held in Chennai in December.
History and Mission
The Thali Awards were founded in 2026 to bridge the gap between architectural design and on-site execution. While traditional architectural awards in India primarily focused on the aesthetic and design aspects of a building, TACA was established with the mission "Honoring the Hands That Build."
The founders sought to acknowledge the "unsung heroes" of the construction sector—specifically the labor force, site supervisors, and structural consultants—whose contributions are critical to the durability and quality of the built environment.
Categories
The awards are divided into four primary zones to cover the lifecycle of a building project. As of 2026, there are 15 distinct categories:
Zone A: Design Excellence
Focuses on the conceptual and aesthetic contributions of principal architects and designers.
The "Namma Veedu" Award: Awarded for the best residential design, split into Urban and Rural sub-categories.
The Green Thali Award: Recognizes excellence in sustainable architecture, specifically the use of eco-friendly materials like compressed earth blocks (CSEB) and bamboo.
Best Commercial Space: For retail and office projects.
Zone B: Execution Heroes
Focuses on the technical realization of the project. This zone is considered the distinguishing feature of the Thali Awards.
The Master Builder Award: Presented to the civil contractor or construction firm demonstrating superior quality of finish and site safety.
The Structural Marvel Award: For structural engineers who have successfully executed projects on challenging terrain or with complex load-bearing requirements.
Restoration Champion: Recognizes teams involved in the conservation of heritage structures, particularly Chettinad architecture and colonial buildings.
Zone C: Craftsmanship
Honors specialized artisans and vendors.
The Golden Trowel: A specific award for masonry and plastering teams.
Best Woodwork & Joinery: For carpenters and interior fabricators.
Material Innovation: For vendors introducing new construction technologies.
Zone D: Future & Community
The Thali Draft: Awarded to the best student thesis from architecture colleges in Tamil Nadu.
Young Architect of the Year: For practicing architects under the age of 30.
Verification Process
Unlike many popularity-based awards, TACA employs a "Site Verification" protocol for its finalists. A technical team, often comprising retired engineers or independent auditors, physically inspects the shortlisted projects to verify construction quality, confirming claims made in the nomination regarding materials and structural integrity.
